clue.text: Shovelhead fools little fish

parts.note: the head of the word Shovel, written as one word with it, is its opening letter
prats is British slang for fools or idiots

explanation.surface: Someone with a shovel-shaped head calls small fish idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shovelhead' looks like one odd word, but split it: the 'head' of 'Shovel' gives its first letter S, then PRATS follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprats are small herring-like sea fish, a standard example of a little fish.

clue.text: Bob found a quicker route

definitions.meaning: a bob is a short haircut
a shorter way to get somewhere

explanation.surface: Bob discovered a faster way to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short cut of hair, and a short cut is also a quicker path.

clue.text: State of health demonstrated by sticking out tongue?

definitions.meaning: rude health means robust health, so the state of being rude in that sense
poking out the tongue is a classic display of bad manners

explanation.surface: A doctor checks your health by asking you to stick out your tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a doctor examining a tongue; but 'rude health' means vigorous health, and sticking out the tongue shows bad manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudeness is impoliteness, as shown by sticking out the tongue, and also the condition of being in rude (robust) health.

clue.text: Pound discovered in bathrobe

indicators.note: discovered in says the answer is found inside the next word, its letters in place

explanation.surface: Money is found in the pocket of a dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money but is a verb, to beat or pulse.
explanation.definitionFit: To throb is to beat heavily, as the heart pounds.

clue.text: Type in a flutter about Grand National?

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the next piece
in a flutter means in a state of agitation, so these letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: G is a common abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Someone is excited about the famous Grand National horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flutter' (with 'in a' as part of the fodder) rearranges TYPEINA to EYPTIAN, and 'about' wraps it round G. 'Grand National' reads as the horse race, but Grand is just G and National is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of Egypt is an Egyptian, so the question mark flags that the answer is one example of a national.

clue.text: Officers' transport in 1926?

parts.note: generals are senior army officers
a trike, a tricycle, is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Senior army officers ride tricycles in 1926.
explanation.walkthrough: The general strike was the British nationwide stoppage of May 1926, when public transport largely stopped, so even generals might need a trike.
explanation.definitionFit: The General Strike was the UK's mass walkout of 1926, so it is what happened in that year.

clue.text: Girl climbing volcano? It's of no great significance

parts.note: Penny is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Etna is a volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: A girl climbing a volcano is said to be nothing much.
explanation.definitionFit: Penny-ante means trivial or small-time, from poker played for tiny stakes.

clue.text: Newspaper supplement, perhaps, is rent asunder

indicators.note: asunder means torn apart, so these letters are pulled into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper's free supplement is torn apart.
explanation.definitionFit: An insert is loose material slipped into a newspaper, a supplement being one example.

clue.text: An enthusiast without a bit of dress sense is seen

definitions.text: An enthusiast without a bit of dress sense is seen

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the enthusiast word goes round the rest

parts.note: a nut is a keen fan, as in a fitness nut

indicators.note: a bit of takes just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A keen fan with no taste in clothes is spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a fan of going without a bit of dress, seen uncovered.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist is an enthusiast for going without clothes, who is seen undressed.

clue.text: Regulated state — alternative to Red Revolution?

parts.note: or introduces an alternative, as in this or that

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters of red are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tidy, well-run society is proposed as the alternative to a Communist uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Revolution' suggests a communist uprising, yet 'Revolution' is only the anagram signal and 'Red' is its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Order is a condition in which everything is regulated and arranged properly.

clue.text: Soon one's buried in church and, having died, is made a saint

indicators.note: buried in means placed inside, so the next pieces sit within the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
anon is an old word for soon
one gives I and the apostrophe s gives S, I'S
D is the standard abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: Someone is soon laid to rest in church and, being dead, is declared a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: The burial in church is apt for a saint, but 'buried in' is simply the container signal; CE (Church of England) is a crossword staple for church.
explanation.definitionFit: To canonise is to declare officially that a dead person is a saint.

clue.text: One fellow's taken another fellow's pigeon? Keats first looked into it

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
man is another word for a fellow, here possessive
a homer is a homing pigeon

explanation.surface: One man has stolen another man's pigeon, with a nod to a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats wrote the sonnet On First Looking into Chapman's Homer, about George Chapman's translation of Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's sonnet title refers to this translation, which he read for the first time.

clue.text: Top man, by not retiring, starts to lack authority, increasing resentment

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the two words by not are read backwards
starts to says take the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: A leader who refuses to step down loses authority as resentment grows.
explanation.walkthrough: BY NOT reversed gives TONYB, then the first letters of lack, authority, increasing and resentment give LAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair was the UK Prime Minister, the top man in British government, from 1997 to 2007, and was much criticised for staying on.

clue.text: Three major engagements here contributing to military presence

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A place where three great battles were fought adds to an army's presence.
explanation.definitionFit: Ypres in Belgium was the site of three major First World War battles, so the place matches three engagements fought there.

clue.text: Man rings club members — that's the procedure with clues like this

annotationWithheld.why: Man rings club members — that's the procedure with clues like this (12): an anagram of MAN RINGS CLUB with no separate indicator; the definition 'that's the procedure with clues like this' also signals the anagram, a phrase doing two jobs, and 'members' has no clear role
annotationWithheld.clue: Man rings club members — that's the procedure with clues like this

clue.text: A couple of chaps not happy in the shade

parts.note: Roy and Al are two men's names
blue means sad

explanation.surface: Two men are unhappy sitting in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep vivid colour, a shade of blue.

clue.text: Bones in the head all turned to point

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: turned means reversed, so all is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Every bone in the head was turned to point a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Patellae are kneecaps, the plural of patella, a bone.

clue.text: I say, lovelorn O'Dowd?

indicators.note: love is O, as zero in tennis, and lorn means lost, so the O is dropped

parts.note: George O'Dowd is the real name of the singer known as Boy George

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims about a lovesick Irishman named O'Dowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Boy George's surname is O'Dowd; 'lovelorn' removes O (love) from BOY GEORGE.
explanation.definitionFit: By George is an old exclamation of surprise, like I say.

clue.text: Under treatment?

parts.note: read as treatment for someone who is put under, that is, sent into a trance, rather than someone being treated by a doctor

explanation.definitionFit: This therapy works by putting the patient into a trance, so the patient is literally under during the treatment.

clue.text: Cast, cast or cast

indicators.note: cast means thrown, so the letters of the words before it are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Three repetitions of one verb make a tongue-twister.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'cast' does three jobs: first the definition (a play's cast), then fodder, then the anagram signal (thrown).
explanation.definitionFit: The cast of a play is its group of actors.

clue.text: Half of Peruvian lake depicted by an old master

indicators.note: half of means only the first part of the lake name is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: Lake Titicaca lies on the border of Peru and Bolivia

explanation.surface: An old master painted part of a South American lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was a great Venetian Renaissance painter, an old master.

clue.text: It's cold on top of Carrock Fell

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a fell is a hill or mountain in northern England

explanation.surface: It is chilly at the summit of a Lake District mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: Carrock Fell is a real Lake District hill, but 'top of' takes only C from Carrock and 'Fell' gives HILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a cold, as in catching a chill, or a feeling of coldness.

clue.text: Aquarius, for example, is a capital enhancement

definitions.meaning: Aquarius is a famous song from the musical Hair, so it is a piece from that show
capital here means head, so this is something that improves the look of the head, a toupee or wig

explanation.surface: A star sign is said to be something that boosts a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A toupee or wig enhances the head (capital), and a number from Hair is literally a Hair piece.

clue.text: Adolescent infatuation with a Turkish official

parts.note: a pash is a schoolgirl or teenage crush

explanation.surface: A teenager falls for a Turkish dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking official in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Banner seen from a mile off

indicators.note: off means wrong or not right, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A flag is visible from a mile away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'a mile off', a distance, but it rearranges FROMAMILE.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriflamme was the red banner of the French kings, and the word is used for any rallying banner.

clue.text: Payment docked for booked swimmer

indicators.note: docked means cut short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: a salary is a regular payment for work

explanation.surface: Someone's wages are cut because they reserved a place in a swimming lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booked' does not mean reserved: the swimmer is one found in the book, i.e. the dictionary, where a salar is a young salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: Salar is a dictionary word for a young salmon, a fish found in reference books, hence a booked swimmer.

clue.text: Small party in Pretoria almost went wrong with wine

parts.note: the ANC, the African National Congress, is the governing party of South Africa, whose capital is Pretoria

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: erred means went wrong or made a mistake

explanation.surface: A minor South African political party got things wrong over wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sancerre is a dry white wine from the Loire valley in France.

clue.text: Challenge issued by Atalanta for flower arrangement?

definitions.meaning: Atalanta of Greek myth challenged her suitors to beat her in a running race
a cluster of flowers arranged on a central stem, the botanical sense

explanation.surface: A mythical runner's dare is said to be a matter of floristry.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is read as two words, RACE ME, Atalanta's dare to her suitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A raceme is a flower cluster with flowers on short stalks along a central stem, a natural flower arrangement.
